title: Ending
description: One SHAPE a run can resolve into, and the clauses that can be assembled behind it (M5 task T61 · FR-STY-06 · GDD Part XIII "Endings philosophy" — there is no single true ending; an ending is assembled from components). Exactly one file per shape: the engine (sim/ending.ts) derives the shape from what the run WAS — not from how it stopped, which is the whole point — then prints the pre-T61 reason scene, this file's `opening`, and the strongest ENDING_CLAUSE_LIMIT clauses whose `when` the run satisfies. Clauses are a MENU, not a template (T87's `accepts` decision applied to prose): the components of a run are thin-and-wide, present in anywhere from 0% to 100% of runs, so a fixed set of sentences would print holes or boilerplate for the ordinary run, while a menu lets a component that is currently unreachable (a companion at your side) be a clause that never fires rather than a gap — and light up with no code change the day it becomes reachable. Price `when` off the measured run, not off the fiction: `measure/t61.ts --components` reports every axis's range and how many runs carry signal on it, and a clause keyed to something measured at 0% is authored for a future the game does not have yet.

requirement.description: A clause's admission test. Every set field must hold; absent fields are ignored (the EncounterRequirement idiom from T47). The vocabulary is closed and engine-side on purpose — content supplies prose and thresholds, the engine supplies the facts.

reasons.description: Run-end reasons this clause is admissible for. Absent means any — and a clause in a shape file is already constrained by the shape, so set this only when the clause names the manner of the ending.

minDays.description: Measured: 1-5 mortal (mean 2.9), 31-44 immortal. A threshold above 5 will not fire in ordinary play today.

minHumanity.description: Absolute standing, 0-100 (baseline 50). Measured range across 200 runs: 31-73 — the authored <=28 and >=85 bands are NOT reachable in play today (PL-M5-69), so prefer the shift fields below for a clause that must actually fire.

minHumanityShift.description: Signed distance from the baseline — the direction of travel. THIS is the axis that moves: 97.5-100% of runs end somewhere other than 50.

minMoralActs.description: `moral` history beats — choices that cost or kept something. Measured 2.35/run, 97.5% of runs.

minMet.description: Survivors met. MEASURED 0.00 IN EVERY POLICY AND BOTH MORTALITY MODES — a clause set on this is authored for later.

minSurvivorsLost.description: `npc.died` beats. Measured 11.9/run mortal; all 18 authored survivors are dead in 100% of immortal runs.

minCompanions.description: Companions standing at the end. MEASURED 0 in 320 runs (T86's PL-M5-63).

minCompanionsLost.description: Measured 0 — nothing is ever recruited to lose.

minRooms.description: Rooms standing in the base at the end. Measured 0-2 (T85).

minFights.description: `combat.cleared`. Measured 5.08/run, 97.5% of runs — one of the liveliest axes there is.

minNodesSeen.description: Nodes entered. Measured 3-7 mortal, 7-31 immortal, of 60.

minNodesCleaned.description: Nodes searched to 100%. Measured 0-4 mortal, 3-21 immortal.

requiresClaimed.description: The run claimed a base at some point — read from the LOG, so a base claimed and later lost still satisfies it.

requiresBaseLost.description: Claimed, and gone by the end (T83's releaseShelter, or an abandon).

requiresBattered.description: Ended carrying wounds, fever, real hunger or real thirst — the pyrrhic read (PL-M5-67). Measured TRUE for 100% of wins, so on a win shape this is the ordinary case and its complement is the rare one.

forbidsBattered.description: Ended clean. The complement of the above, so the rare good end can be authored without a second vocabulary.

requiresAlone.description: No companion at the end. Measured true for 100% of runs today.

requiresFeverish.description: Ended with the infection past `none`. Narrower than requiresBattered on purpose — "you got out and it came with you" is a different ending from "you got out hurt". Measured: infection.staged fires in 95% of runs.

maxBreached.description: Upper bound on `siege.breached` beats. The only max on a count in this vocabulary: losing a base to a breach and losing one any other way are different stories, and a clause about the general case should not print beside the specific one that caused it.

requiresAtBase.description: The survivor was standing in a base they STILL HELD when the run stopped. Distinct from requiresClaimed, which is historical — owning a fortified base is not the same as dying in its doorway.

forbidsClaimed.description: The run never claimed a base at all. The vocabulary is otherwise monotone, so this is how a clause about being rootless is kept off a survivor who settled on day 2.

standActs.description: Act ids the run's final turn may have been spent on (M5 task T62). Absent means any, INCLUDING a run that took no act at all — so a clause that sets this never fires for a run played without a content/stands/ pool. This is how the Last Stand's choice reaches the closing prose: a clause can name what the survivor DID rather than only what was true of them. Ids are the bare act ids as authored in content/stands/ (hold-the-line, leave-what-you-carry, take-it-with-you, leave-the-mark, say-it, ...) plus the engine's own floor act `stand.let-go`.

id.description: Stable slug, unique within this ending. Not save data (nothing about an ending is stored) but it IS the trail tests and telemetry read, so treat it as stable.

weight.description: Selection order — higher wins a contested slot, ties break on id so selection is total and machine-independent. Supply usually exceeds ENDING_CLAUSE_LIMIT, so this is the dial that decides which truths about a run get said.

text.description: Second-person past-tense prose, one or two sentences, no numbers and no scoreboard (GDD XIII: every ending gets a real close, not a card). It is read AFTER the reason scene and the opening, so it should add a fact about the run rather than re-narrate the death.

$schema.description: Optional editor hint pointing at this schema.

shape.description: GDD XIII's four shapes. UNIQUE ACROSS THE POOL — buildRegionGraph refuses two defs claiming the same shape, because a run resolves into one shape and must find one def (a JSON Schema validates one file at a time and cannot see the collision).

opening.description: The line that names what this run WAS. Printed whenever the pool is live, immediately after the reason scene, before any clause.

clauses.description: The candidate sentences. Author MORE than ENDING_CLAUSE_LIMIT — the cap binding is what makes two runs of the same shape differ instead of converging on everything that was true of you. A clause with no `when` is unconditional and will crowd the list at equal weight, so give those a low weight and use them as the floor. The ceiling was raised from 24 to 32 by T62 for a measured reason: making `sacrifice` reachable from anywhere in the city and from all four deaths (it had been reachable only at your own door, and therefore not at all) meant every clause in that file that quietly assumed a base had to be gated, which left a rootless survivor four admissible clauses against a cap of three — and the distinct-text count FELL, 22 Last Stand texts to 17. It recovered to 27 only once the shape carried the same spread of run-fact clauses `fade` already had. REACHING A SHAPE COSTS CONTENT: the thinner the gate, the more sentences it needs behind it.
